title: Summarize Various Security Measures and Their Purposes

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Security works best in layers. Organizations protect people, facilities, systems, accounts, applications, and data with physical, logical, identity, and data-protection controls.
Use this mental model: keep them away → verify who they are → limit what they can do → protect the data.
bullets: Privilege, endpoint, data, identity, and directory controls

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a security requirement appears, identify what is being protected: the facility, physical entry, an identity, a logical resource, privileged access, an endpoint, or sensitive data.
sections.callout: Stop vehicles → bollards; verify every request → Zero Trust; minimum permissions → least privilege; stop sensitive-data leakage → DLP.

sections.title: Physical Security
paragraphs: Physical security protects facilities, equipment, and people from unauthorized physical access, theft, and damage.

entries.title: Bollards
paragraphs: Strong posts or barriers that stop or redirect vehicles around entrances and sensitive areas.

entries.title: Access Control Vestibule
paragraphs: A two-door controlled space that verifies a person before releasing the second door and helps prevent tailgating.

entries.title: Badge Reader
paragraphs: Reads an employee or visitor credential to unlock a door, record entry, or enforce role-based physical access.

entries.title: Video Surveillance
paragraphs: Monitors and records activity to deter wrongdoing, support investigations, and provide evidence.

entries.title: Alarm Systems
paragraphs: Alert personnel when a door, glass-break sensor, or other monitored condition indicates possible unauthorized entry.

entries.title: Motion Sensors
paragraphs: Detect movement and can trigger lights, alarms, or recording.

entries.title: Door Locks
paragraphs: Physically restrict entry to rooms or buildings.

entries.title: Equipment Locks
paragraphs: Physically secure laptops, computers, and other valuable devices.
entries.recognitionCue: Keep a device from walking away → equipment lock.

entries.title: Security Guards
paragraphs: Provide human verification, patrol, enforcement, and incident response.

entries.title: Fences
paragraphs: Define a perimeter and deter or delay unauthorized entry.

sections.title: Physical Access Security
paragraphs: Physical access controls determine who may cross a physical security boundary.

entries.title: Key Fobs
paragraphs: Electronic credentials presented to an access-control reader.
entries.recognitionCue: Tap or present a fob → access.

entries.title: Smart Cards
paragraphs: Chip-based cards that store or process authentication information for building access, computer authentication, or identity verification.

entries.title: Mobile Digital Key
paragraphs: Allows a phone or other mobile device to act as an access credential.

entries.title: Keys
paragraphs: Traditional physical keys operate locks but can be lost, copied, or stolen.

sections.title: Biometrics
paragraphs: Biometrics verify identity using a biological or behavioral characteristic: something you are.

entries.title: Retina Scanner
paragraphs: Analyzes characteristics inside the eye.

entries.title: Fingerprint Scanner
paragraphs: Analyzes fingerprint patterns.

entries.title: Palm Print Scanner
paragraphs: Analyzes characteristics of the user's palm.

entries.title: Facial Recognition Technology (FRT)
paragraphs: Compares facial characteristics.

entries.title: Voice Recognition Technology
paragraphs: Authenticates from characteristics of a person's voice.

entries.title: Lighting
paragraphs: Improves visibility, strengthens surveillance, deters intrusion, and removes dark hiding places.

entries.title: Magnetometers
paragraphs: Detect metal objects during security screening.

sections.title: Logical Security
paragraphs: Logical controls protect systems, applications, accounts, networks, and data.

entries.title: Principle of Least Privilege
paragraphs: Give a user or process only the access needed to perform its job.

entries.title: Zero Trust Model
paragraphs: Do not automatically trust a user, device, or request because it is inside the network; verify explicitly and continuously.
entries.recognitionCue: Should this request be trusted? Verify it.

entries.title: Access Control Lists (ACLs)
paragraphs: Allow or deny specified users, groups, systems, or traffic access to a resource.
entries.recognitionCue: Who or what is allowed? → ACL.

sections.title: Multifactor Authentication (MFA)
paragraphs: MFA combines factors from more than one category, such as something you know, have, and are. Two passwords are not MFA because they are the same factor type.

entries.title: Email
paragraphs: Delivers an authentication code or confirmation through email.

entries.title: Hardware Token
paragraphs: A physical device used as an authentication factor.

entries.title: Authenticator Application
paragraphs: Generates a code or receives an approval request on a registered device.

entries.title: Short Message Service (SMS)
paragraphs: Delivers a code by text message.

entries.title: Voice Call
paragraphs: Calls a registered number to confirm authentication.

entries.title: Time-Based One-Time Password (TOTP)
paragraphs: Generates a short-lived code using the current time, commonly changing every 30 seconds.

entries.title: One-Time Password/Passcode (OTP)
paragraphs: A broad category of codes valid for one authentication event or a short period; TOTP is one way to create an OTP.

sections.title: SAML and Single Sign-On

entries.title: Security Assertions Markup Language (SAML)
paragraphs: Exchanges identity and authentication assertions between systems and commonly enables federated web authentication.

entries.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
paragraphs: Lets a user authenticate once and access multiple authorized services without repeated sign-ins.

sections.callout: SSO is the user capability; SAML is one technology that can enable federated SSO.

entries.title: Just-in-Time Access
paragraphs: Grants elevated rights only when needed and for a limited period.

entries.title: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
paragraphs: Controls and monitors administrator credentials, elevated sessions, temporary access, and privileged activity.

entries.title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
paragraphs: Centrally applies device settings, application controls, compliance rules, and remote lock or wipe actions to mobile endpoints.
entries.recognitionCue: Manage company phones and tablets → MDM.

entries.title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
paragraphs: Detects or blocks sensitive information from leaving approved locations or being shared improperly.

entries.title: Identity Access Management (IAM)
paragraphs: The broad framework for identities, authentication, authorization, and access.
entries.recognitionCue: Who are you and what may you access? → IAM.

entries.title: Directory Services
paragraphs: Centrally store and organize users, groups, computers, and resources; Active Directory is an example.
entries.recognitionCue: Central identity and resource store → directory service.

rows: IAM is the broader identity framework
IAM manages identity and access processes

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Controlled two-door entry → access control vestibule

sections.title: Objective 2.1 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Answer the control named by the scenario's purpose, not merely a related security term.
bullets: Least privilege limits access; Zero Trust questions every request.
OTP means one use; TOTP is specifically time generated.
SAML is an assertion technology; SSO is the one-login experience.
JIT provides temporary elevation; PAM manages privileged accounts and sessions.
MDM manages devices; DLP protects sensitive data from leaving.
Directory services store identities; IAM governs identity and access.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: Keep them away → verify them → limit them → protect the data.
